requirements.requirement: Run inventory-api as a managed service on node1, listening on TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: A systemd unit was created, enabled, and started. Direct checks showed it active under the inventory-api account, owning 0.0.0.0:8080, and returning successful health and inventory responses both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Limit the separate batchworker account to 128 MB of virtual memory per process and ensure a failed batch allocation does not interrupt the API.
requirements.summary: The separate batchworker account had soft and hard address-space limits of 134,217,728 bytes (128 MiB). A bounded 200 MiB allocation failed with MemoryError while API health was directly observed before and after the failure; the same behavior remained after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 from baseline through final observation. The implementation used the already-installed Python 3 runtime, added no packages, ran successfully, and package-manager consistency remained healthy.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, reboot was acknowledged and observed, the boot ID changed, and the service, listener, inventory data, memory limit, allocation isolation, OS, and kernel were healthy afterward. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account, data, application, service, and limit-file creation directly supported the requested outcomes; the reboot scheduling was necessary for the provider restart protocol and used transient runtime units. Allocation testing was bounded and transient. Final observations showed no failed services, healthy package state, and only expected reboot-generated private temporary directories. The new TCP 8080 listener was required by the task.
